question: A shopkeeper buys a note book for ₹85. He wants a profit of 20% after giving a discount of 15%. At what price should he mark the note book?
solution:
**(SP-CP)/(CP)Given:**

Cost Price of notebook = Rs 85

Discount% = 15%

Profit% = 20%

**Concept Used:**

Profit% = (SP-CP)/(CP)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the marked price of a notebook be Rs x

⇒ Discount on the notebook = x – 0.15x = Rs 0.85x

⇒ Selling Price of a notebook = Rs 0.85x

⇒ Putting the value in the Profit% formula,

⇒ Profit% = (0.85x-85)/(85)

⇒ (20)/(100)=(0.85x-85)/(85)

⇒ 0.85x-85=17

⇒ x=(102)/(0.85)=120

**Hence, the marked price of the notebook will be Rs 120**
